newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta share prices end lower but off lows.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta share prices end lower but off lows.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended lower but off their lows on Wednesday, dragged down by profit-taking in blue chip counters, particularly in heavyweight Telkom, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index closed down 4.86 points, or 0.70 percent, at 693.54 after hitting a low for the day of 690.52 points.
Losers led gainers by 63 to 52, with 77 counters unchanged. Turn-over was estimated at 563 billion rupiah, compared to 568 billion rupiah on Tuesday.
Brokers said the market was likely to be mixed on Thursday on possible follow-through profit-taking after recent sharp gains and also due to the lack of strong fresh news in the market.

Brokers also said trading volume was likely to be modest as investors remain concerned over possible post-election disturbances after two minority parties alleged there had been widespread election irregularities.
"But intense market speculation on some counters such as Surya Semesta and Mas Murni might continue to draw attention," one local broker said.
Property firm Surya Semesta rose 50 rupiah to 1,225 rupiah in active trading of 29.5 million shares.
Brokers said it was boosted by strong market talk that a local conglomerate or foreign investors might take a stake in the firm.
"Aside from all the rumours, its fundamentals have also improved," a local broker said.
Surya announced on Tuesday it had net profit of 28.28 billion rupiah in the first quarter of 1997 against a net loss of 10.03 billion rupiah in the corresponding period in 1996.

Ceramic tile producer Intikeramik was the most active stock on its debut on Wednesday with about 60 million shares changing hands. It was last traded at 925 rupiah, compared to its offer price of 750 rupiah.
Blue chips Telkom closed 100 rupiah lower at 4,000 rupiah, Semen Gresik 125 rupiah off at 5,500 rupiah and Astra International down 125 rupiah at 6,925 rupiah.

Media reports quoting Trade and Industry Minister Tungky Aribowo as saying government organisations might soon have to buy a "national car" produced by a firm controlled by one of President Suharto's sons to boost sales, helped dampen sentiment on Astra International and Bimantara which also produces a similar type of sedan.
"But today's fall in Astra was more due to a sharp recent rise which had been boosted by its plan for a stock split," a broker with a foreign firm said.
